text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: SSE/streaming degradations detected for /v1/stream (tool-call payloads). P95 latency for SSE clients > 10s, several 499 disconnects. Impact: some customers report tool-call parse failures. Auto-page to oncall.

maya: ack — I'm on it. I'm pulling logs and attaching trace ids. If anyone is oncall for infra handoff ping now.

jordan: I'm available. What are we seeing for error classes? 5xx from edge or client 499s?

elena: initial look: edge shows a burst of 502s and then a high rate of client-side disconnects (499) during the streaming handshake. Model serving shows occasional tool-call partial frames that fail JSON parsing on the client. Sample log: 

```
2026-03-15T13:02:12Z INFO stream_conn id=abcd1234 state=init
2026-03-15T13:02:16Z WARN frame_parse id=abcd1234 reason=truncated_payload
2026-03-15T13:02:16Z ERROR tool_call id=abcd1234 payload='{"tool":"search","args":{...}}' parse_error=Unexpected end of JSON input
```

maya: customer-reported example from neil (CS): they saw "tool.call.parseError: Unexpected token" and then the client retried and got empty streaming body.

neil: correct. Customer is on adopter plan, experiencing failed tool responses when using SSE-based streaming + function-calls. They reported the timeline started ~13:02 UTC and lasted ~8 minutes.

ryan: hypothesis 1: upstream NLB/proxy dropped long-lived SSE connections under load -> clients closed and got 499s. Hypothesis 2: partial frames emitted by runtime due to batching/kv-cache race -> client JSON parse errors. We should track both.

jordan: adding quick checks: CPU on serving nodes at spike time? Any OOMs? Any kernel-level drops?

elena: serving CPU spiked on a subset of pods at 13:01:50, but pod memory fine. There's a pattern: pods that handled long sequences rolled their event loop and emitted partial frames while a background KV snapshot occurred. That aligns with partial JSON bodies.

maya: mitigation options: 1) Enable SSE keepalive pings for affected edge route (reduce client timeouts). 2) Temporary route affected customers to non-streaming polled endpoint (fallback). 3) Roll restart subset of serving pods to clear event-loop backpressure. Which can we do fast?

ryan: I can flip keepalive on edge in ~2 minutes (config change on proxy). Rolling restart of 10% of the serving pool can be done; will do canary then widen.

jordan: while that happens, elena, can you dump the raw frames (hex or base64) for a few trace ids so we can confirm partial JSON boundaries? Put them in the incident channel.

elena: dumping now for ids abcd1234, ef56gh78. Paste below (base64 to keep formatting):
```
abcd1234: eyJ0b29sIjogInNlYXJjaCIsICJhcmdzIjogeyJxdWVyeSI6ICJmaWx0ZXIifX0KewoK
ef56gh78: eyJ0b29sIjogInBpbmciLCAiYXJncyI6IHsiayI6ICJ2YWx1ZSJ9fQ==
```
(note: those decode to fragments; second one missing trailing brackets occasionally)

neil: customer is asking for ETA for mitigation — can we give a short window?

maya: ETA for keepalive flip + deploy: 5-8 minutes. Rolling restart/clear backlog: 15-25 minutes. We'll update by +10.

incident-bot: oncall handoff reminder: maya is primary until 1780045800; next oncall: jordan at 1780045800. Use /handoff when ready.

jordan: observed new 499 spike aligned with proxy worker restarts at 13:03:20. Proxy logs show a transient resource exhaustion on that AZ. Looks like clients that had partial frames interpreted as EOF.

ryan: keepalive enabled for route. I also raised the proxy connection timeout from 60s to 120s for streaming endpoints as temporary.

elena: confirm: after keepalive flip, ERROR tool_call parse errors drop from 40/min to ~5/min in the next minute window. Partial frames still show up for some trace ids; pushing canary restart of two pods to clear event-loop state.

maya: canary restart started. neil, please tell customer we did a hotfix: keepalive + proxy timeout increase, and we're restarting a small subset of serving pods to remove partial-frame backlog. Apologize and offer to switch them to polled endpoint if they prefer immediate stable behavior.

neil: relayed to customer — they took fallback and are stable for now. They asked for a root cause writeup and whether this will recur.

elena: timeline draft (in-thread):
- 13:01:42 UTC: spike in long-tail requests to /v1/stream (client retry storm from downstream integration)
- 13:01:50 UTC: subset of serving pods CPU climbs due to heavy KV/cache work; event loop delays observed
- 13:02:12 UTC: partial frames emitted and clients see truncated JSON -> parse errors
- 13:02:16 UTC: proxy workers reach resource threshold and restart, many SSE clients receive 499s
- 13:03:20 UTC: keepalive enabled and proxy timeout increased (mitigation 1)
- 13:04:10 UTC: canary restarts performed (mitigation 2)
- 13:10:00 UTC: metrics trending back to baseline; customer fallbacks stable

jordan: hypothesis list (we'll mark and track):
H1 (probable): Event-loop backpressure in runtime during KV snapshot/batching caused partial frame emission. This plus proxy restarts caused client parse errors and 499s.
H2 (contrib): Proxy worker resource exhaustion amplified client disconnects under retry storms.
H3 (unlikely): Client library incompatibility with chunked SSE edge cases. We haven't seen different clients fail consistently (one customer did), but need to validate across SDK versions.

elena: experiments to run:
- Reproduce in staging with synthetic retry storm and KV snapshot schedule.
- Add stricter per-frame validation on runtime side to avoid emitting partial JSON frames (fail rather than send incomplete).
- Add streaming healthcheck to edge to avoid worker restarts during bursts.

maya: immediate action items (assigned):
- r1 (elena): collect more frame dumps and add to ticket INC-1780045600. Mark whether frames end with newline/\n. (owner)
- r2 (ryan): keepalive toggle + proxy timeout reverted to original after stability window. (owner)
- r3 (jordan): run staging repro and confirm H1. (owner)
- r4 (neil): coordinate with customer and capture SDK version + exact client stack. (owner)
- r5 (maya): write incident summary and schedule post-incident RCA meeting 1hr. (owner)

incident-bot: NOTE: create-incident-ticket INC-1780045600 — link https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1780045600

liz: small ask: let's add a compatibility note to the SDK docs about streaming resilient handling (auto-retry vs. polled fallback). Might reduce customer retry storms that amplify this.

maya: agreed. We'll add doc note in next SDK patch. Jordan, once you confirm repro, schedule a dedicated follow-up to propose runtime fixes (frame validation, safer batching during KV snapshots).

jordan: ack. I'll pick this up in 10m and update thread with staging results.

elena: one more detail: tool-call parsing errors came from frames missing terminal newline delimiter. We should standardize on fixed delimiter handshake in protocol v1.1 to help client libs detect incomplete frames earlier. Adding to action items.

neil: customer pleased with temporary fix and wants timeline + RCA once ready. They also asked if we can provide logs for their trace ids — will attach when we export them to secure bucket.

maya: handing off now to jordan (per incident-bot). jordan, you're primary. I'll stay available for questions. /handoff 

jordan: thanks. taking primary. Will post staging repro results and draft RCA here.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> reduced errors, some customers on fallback. Please update ticket INC-1780045600 with any follow-ups.

maya: closing communication loop for oncall; good job team. We'll run formal RCA and postmortem with timeline and code/infra mitigations.

jordan: update (post-canary): staging repro shows same partial-frame behavior when our KV snapshot overlaps with heavy batching. Repro steps and logs uploaded to INC-1780045600. Next up: design change to avoid emitting partial frames (elena + eng-runtime).

elena: copy. I'll start a RFC for frame validation and a small runtime change to ensure atomic frame emission.

neil: customer notified. They appreciate the prompt mitigation.

maya: end of thread — will attach final RCA draft to the ticket in ~1h.
